transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Wu (Redwood SE), Markus Feld (Peregrine Infra Lead), Sana Iqbal (Peregrine SRE), Liam O'Connor (Product), Aisha Romero (Security)

Summary (auto): quick hands-on lab to validate request replay, hypothesis-driven debugging using Console traces and breakpoints, discuss data handling and dedicated capacity tradeoffs.

Topics: replay workflow, trace breakpoints, KV cache mis-hits, error-rate triage, SOC2/KMS questions, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intro? I'm Jordan with Redwood, AE. Priya and Daniel from our observability team are on. 
[00:06] Markus: Hey all, Markus here, infra. We're focused on an intermittent 5-10% latency spike that coincides with some upstream timeouts.
[00:12] Sana: yeah hi, Sana SRE. we've got replay logs and a sample trace set.
[00:15] Jordan: perfect. goal for today is to run a replay hypothesis lab in the Console so we can exercise the exact request paths and show how breakpoints and trace playbacks help isolate the error clause. also cover data protection and dedicated options. sound good?
[00:24] Liam: yes that sounds great. curious about the dedicated pool sizing too.
[00:27] Priya: ok, i'll drive the console demo, show the trace map, then we’ll drop in breakpoints and replay a subset. fair warning transcription may spell some product names funny — e.g., the runtime shows up as Redwood Opti-mize in some logs, you'll see variants.
[00:38] [00:38] Priya: hopping into the Console now, i've loaded the request inspector view. you can see the request timeline on the left, each token timing, prefix cache hits — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — you'll see those hits/misses.
[00:52] [00:52] Priya: here's a sample trace where the downstream call to our recommendation microservice times out at ~280ms and then the runtime falls back to a smaller model variant which increases token generation time.
[01:05] Sana: is that automatic fallback? we thought fallback was only configured for canary routes.
[01:09] Priya: by default we have a policy that allows model variant fallback to keep tail latency bounded; can be disabled per route. you can see the policy in the trace metadata — it's tagged as "fallback_policy: smart_route_v2" but speech-to-text sometimes shows it as fall back police.
[01:22] Daniel: i'll point out the trace correlation id at top is the same as in your replay batch.csv — that's how we stitch logs across services.
[01:29] Markus: curious: when you replay, does it reconstruct KV cache state? we found cache warmup matters.
[01:34] Priya: good question. the replay tool replays requests but doesn't automatically reconstruct remote KV cache unless you enable prefix/KV recording and restore. we have a 'cache-priming' mode in the Console that will run a quick warmup before the replay.
[01:46] [01:46] Priya: ok dropping in a breakpoint at the downstream call boundary — look at the callout. breakpoint allows you to pause and inject a synthetic response so you can confirm whether the downstream timeout is the root cause.
[01:58] Liam: can you show the step where we drop in a synthetic 200 vs a slow 500 to see how the Redwood runtime reacts?
[02:03] Priya: yep. running first with a synthetic slow response — watch how the overall token generation stalls and then the runtime triggers the fallback. note the trace shows kv cache miss, and there's a small spike in token compute time.
[02:18] [02:18] Priya: now inject a positive synthetic response — that path completes under target SLO and no fallback. so hypothesis: intermittent downstream slow responses -> fallback -> longer gen time -> visible latency spikes.
[02:30] Markus: ok makes sense. is there telemetry to measure how often fallback happens and cost impact?
[02:35] Daniel: yes, in Console you get per-route metrics: fallback rate, average token cost, model-switch count. our Optimize tab will suggest quantization or batching tweaks to reduce cost when fallback increases token churn.
[02:46] Aisha: from a security POV we need to know if replayed traffic leaves our VPC or touches Redwood logs in a way that could include PII.
[02:53] Jordan: great point. short answer: hosted replay uses Redwood's secure path by default and you can enable customer-managed VPC for Private deployments. we keep replay payloads encrypted at rest and in transit; SOC2 docs give the specifics. i'll send the SOC2 + KMS brief after the call. transcription might show "KMS" as K M S or K M S key, just FYI.
[03:10] Aisha: and retention? we need to avoid storing traces with PII.
[03:13] Priya: Console has redaction hooks and we support on-the-fly PII scrubbing via regex rules before storing traces. you can also set retention windows per namespace; we recommend short retention for sensitive flows.
[03:23] Sana: for the replay, we can redact at source and provide sanitized traffic capture. we'll share that.
[03:27] [03:27] Priya: ok next, i'll run a 1k-request replay from your uploaded capture (name shows up as peregine_capture.csv in the UI, sometimes STT mangles it to peregrine). starting now, enabling cache-priming.
[03:40] [03:40] Priya: replay progress bar at 25%. you'll notice the Console logs list request-level timings; there is also a flamegraph view showing where time is spent: token decode, model forward, network wait for downstream svc.
[03:55] Priya: here at 42% we see a cluster of slow tails — grouping by correlation id shows it's the same downstream endpoint. i'll mark those as suspect and create a hypothesis filter.
[04:08] Liam: can the filter be exported to our SRE toolchain? we use PagerX.
[04:12] Daniel: yes you can export a list of correlation ids and timestamps as CSV. integration with PagerX via webhook is supported for alert enrichment.
[04:21] [04:21] Priya: small hiccup in demo video feed — sorry, my console had a lag.
[04:26] Jordan: no worries. while priya recovers, quick qualification question — what's your preferred deployment path? are you leaning hosted first or do you want Private/VPC from day one?
[04:35] Markus: we prefer hosted for initial eval but need VPC path by pilot. security needs SSO/SAML and HSM/KMS support.
[04:41] Aisha: yes SSO + audit logs are critical; also need to know where logs live.
[04:44] Jordan: we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, and detailed audit logs in both Hosted and Private. for on-prem or air-gapped we provide a packaging option with customer-managed keywrapping. i'll attach the deployment checklist.
[04:55] Priya: back — replay finished. overall fallback rate was 8.2% in this run, average p95 increased by ~210ms on affected requests. i'm uploading the replay results and heatmap.
[05:07] Priya: drill into a slow sample, you can see token-by-token timing: token 1-50 are fine, at token ~73 there's a 180ms pause waiting for upstream. speech to text sometimes shows 'token pause' as 'taken pause'.
[05:20] Sana: is there a way to tune fallback thresholds so we don't flip to a smaller variant on transient blips?
[05:25] Priya: yes you can configure route-level thresholds: e.g., require consecutive failures N within T seconds before fallback. you can also set a latency budget to prefer timeouts over fallback.
[05:36] Markus: what about cost? switching variants increases tokens and cost, right?
[05:40] Daniel: correct, fallback can increase token consumption because sometimes the smaller model performs more decoding steps for the same output, and if you re-request you double-count tokens. Console's Optimize module will estimate cost delta and suggest batching/quant profiles to mitigate.
[05:55] [05:55] Priya: showing the Optimize suggestion panel now — for your workload it recommends enabling prefix cache for routes X and Y, and a 4x request batching window during off-peak. it also suggests switching one route from fp16 to int8 quant which reduces latency on T4-like infra.
[06:11] Liam: model quantization concerns the accuracy of outputs. have you seen regressions?
[06:15] Priya: we run A/B eval sets — Optimize shows expected quality delta. for many instruction-style prompts the int8 delta is negligible; we include a quality sandbox to validate.
[06:24] Aisha: will those evals or logs include our sample text? we need to ensure eval data is private.
[06:29] Jordan: evals run in a customer-scoped environment and data remains in your namespace — but we'll share the exact data flow diagram in the security brief.
[06:38] [06:38] Priya: ok switching to request-forensics flow: when you click a trace and choose 'replay with breakpoint', we capture a forked execution trace and you can compare before/after timelines side-by-side. it's handy for root-cause once you hypothesize a downstream fault.
[06:51] Sana: nice. can we automate alerts when a new spike pattern appears?
[06:55] Daniel: yes, there's anomaly detectors you can train on token-level latency signatures. they can trigger external webhooks or create incidents in PagerX.
[07:04] Markus: about dedicated pools — if we go dedicated, do we get pinned GPUs and guaranteed KV cache?
[07:09] Priya: Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and can pin model variants to instances for warm cache. you still retain the same Console and control plane; the difference is isolated capacity and predictable throughput.
[07:20] Markus: what's the SLA?
[07:23] Jordan: Dedicated SLAs started at 99.9% and we offer escalation paths for enterprise. SLA details will be in the dedicated contract appendix I'll share.
[07:33] [07:33] Priya: small demo tangent — i'm toggling a request to show 'trace playbook' where we attach a remediation script that can be triggered automatically if a breakpoint identifies a recurring timeout. it can, for example, re-route a route to a different region.
[07:47] Liam: interesting — does re-routing preserve session context? we need to ensure in-flight user conversations don't lose state.
[07:52] Priya: we preserve KV keys and session metadata; re-route is at the model-routing layer so the session tokens are forwarded. there are caveats for region-bound data, but that's surfaced in the playbook config.
[08:05] Aisha: about audit logs and evidence for compliance — do you keep immutable copies or can customers export them?
[08:11] Daniel: you can get an export; in Private/VPC mode logs can be shipped to your S3 or SIEM via secure connectors. we also support write-once retention for audit evidence.
[08:23] Jordan: quick pause for questions. anything else red team-wise?
[08:26] Aisha: just to confirm HSM integration for key wrapping?
[08:29] Jordan: yes, we integrate with major cloud HSMs and can support BYOK (bring your own key) for Private deployments. note in hosted we can offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KEK if that's approved.
[08:42] Priya: demo note: some terms in the transcript may appear as 'break point' or 'break point trace' merged, or 'KV' as 'K V'. apologies for STT artifacts.
[08:49] [08:49] Priya: showing final replay summary: 1k requests, 82 fallback events, p95 delta +210ms, estimated incremental monthly cost if unaddressed ~$4.8k. Optimize suggests prefix caching and raising the fallback threshold to bring fallback to <1%.
[09:03] Markus: can you reduce fallback while keeping latency SLO?
[09:06] Priya: yes: combine a slightly higher fallback threshold with preemptive cache priming and a short client-side retry window. that keeps SLO while avoiding model switches for single blips.
[09:17] Daniel: for the pilot we'd recommend a 2-week replay + live canary where we measure fallbacks and cost delta.
[09:23] Jordan: next steps recap: we'll run an extended 1k/5k replay with your redacted capture, share the replay heatmap, security brief, and pricing sketches. we'll plan a dedicated sizing deep dive if pilot metrics warrant.
[09:36] Liam: sounds good. Markus/Sana will assemble the sanitized capture and policy.
[09:41] Markus: yes we'll have that to you by Friday.
[09:44] Aisha: expecting SOC2, KMS, retention diagram from Jordan.
[09:47] Jordan: yep will send during EOD Thursday.
[09:51] Priya: final note: Console has a 'playback audit' view that shows who ran replays and which keys were used — useful for compliance reviews.
[09:59] Sana: great, appreciate the walkthrough.
[10:02] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcription.
